external_invariants: Model is ResNetForImageClassification loaded from the local assets directory only (local_files_only=True) in float32; no downloads.
All weights and activations remain FP32; torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 and torch.backends.cudnn.allow_tf32 are False and torch.set_float32_matmul_precision('highest').
Seed policy: torch.manual_seed(20261020) applied in prepare, matching common.configure().

Input is the real preprocessed image fixture tensor from assets/pixels.npy (3 images, NCHW float32), selected as images[torch.arange(batch) % len(images)].contiguous(); for the frozen 'online' workload batch=1, i.e. the first image, unchanged every repeat.
The model is in eval() mode and the forward pass runs under torch.inference_mode(), identical to the source infer() helper calling model(pixel_values=pixels).logits.
Batch size is fixed at 1 for this workload; the workload, data, precision and output requirements are not altered to improve the score.
Correctness requires all logits within atol=1e-4 / rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 argmax equality against the reference; observations include every logit and the predicted class integer.

Latency is wall time around run() with CUDA synchronization at both boundaries, per the source's per-repeat timing; throughput is derived from the unchanged work amount (batch=1) and the measured elapsed time.
The adapter does not initialize CUDA or load the model at import time and never destroys the process group in reset.

selection.rationale: Repair of rejected trial-61aff8484b, which selected group 5621410346ca09a421d0 (three stage-4 stride-1 [1,512,7,7]x[512,512,3,3] convs) and replaced them with an im2col+cuBLAS-GEMM composite. That trial passed quality (max_abs_error 3.9e-6, exact top-1, full coverage) but regressed the project objective from 1.446/1.453 ms to 4.863/4.941 ms (paired gains -3.416/-3.488 ms against MAD noise bounds 0.121/0.335 ms; rejected for paired_gain_not_above_noise and objective_not_improved). The measured lesson: clean wall latency (~1.45 ms) is about 2x total GPU busy time (~0.73 ms diagnostic, 81/81 kernels associated), so this single-device batch=1 workload is dispatch/launch-bound; per-call CPU-side composite work (extra aten dispatches, views, closures across three replacement sites) and a slow no-TF32 skinny-N batched-GEMM route can dominate any kernel-time saving, and im2col+matmul composites are refuted as a mechanism here. The repaired selection therefore moves to the largest untried leaf group with the worst measured kernel efficiency and the smallest structural risk: fc4ee42c1ef82b000685, a single call (faf88ed785916744a12ba5c9) of aten::conv2d with input [1,256,14,14] (stride [50176,196,14,1]), weight [512,256,3,3] (stride [2304,9,3,1]), stride [2,2], padding [1,1], dilation [1,1], groups 1, bias None, producing the stage-3->4 transition tensor [1,512,7,7]. It costs 115.5 diagnostic CUDA us (15.9% of the 727.7 us run total; second-largest leaf group, and the largest never-attempted one) in a single kernel, implicit_convolve_sgemm<float,...,128,5,5,3,3,3,1,...>, launched with grid [2,16] x block [8,8] = 32 CTAs / 2048 threads, i.e. severe shape-driven under-occupancy (49 output positions tile into too few CTAs), yielding ~1.00 TFLOP/s FP32 for its 115.6 MFLOP. Direct controls inside the same forward pass prove the headroom on this exact device and FLOP budget: the same-kernel-family stride-2 downsample convs 63a5f3f5517368acbd7e625c (128->256, out 14x14, grid [7,8]) and 8344cbbcd6c950f8dab33c94 (64->128, out 28x28, grid [25,4]) compute the identical 115.6 MFLOP in 36.2 us (3.19 TFLOP/s) and 30.6 us (3.78 TFLOP/s), and the Winograd-served stride-1 group 7fb0d2de3e359d451ab3 reaches 6.8 TFLOP/s. A single-call boundary is a coherent editable surface (one dispatch site in the ResNetStage-3 shortcut path) with no co-dependent edits, and one replacement site bounds the aggregate per-call overhead that invalidated the previous three-site trial. Implementation constraints carried from the failure evidence: the replacement must stay a single kernel launch / single dispatch for the guarded signature (no im2col+GEMM, no per-call Python tensor reshaping or view construction; any weight repacking or plan setup happens once at build time outside timing), must keep TF32 disabled, cudnn.benchmark False and all global flags untouched, and must carry a strict signature guard falling back to the parent aten::conv2d for any other signature. Diagnostic CUDA durations are nested/inclusive and hook-perturbed; they justify only the ranking, not a predicted wire-time gain.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing the single [1,256,14,14]x[512,256,3,3] stride-2/pad-1/bias-None convolution (call faf88ed785916744a12ba5c9) with a single-launch, occupancy-aware FP32 implementation for exactly this signature - while keeping cudnn.benchmark False, TF32 disabled, logits within atol=rtol=1e-4 and exact top-1 - will move its cost from 115.5 us toward the 30-36 us its same-FLOP, same-kernel-family sibling convolutions already achieve in the same forward pass, removing roughly 80-85 us of serialized GPU critical path (~11-12% of the 727.7 us diagnostic run total). Because the previous trial proved wall latency is dispatch-bound (1.45 ms wall vs 0.73 ms GPU busy), the realized latency_ms gain may be smaller than the kernel saving and must exceed the paired AB/BA MAD-derived noise bounds (0.121-0.335 ms) to be accepted; the replacement therefore adds no per-call CPU-side dispatch beyond the original single call. This is a hypothesis to be tested by the framework's independent paired measurement, not a predicted benefit: if the single-kernel route does not clear the noise bounds, the fallback is to reject rather than to expand into multi-op composites, which are now measured to regress this workload.

proposal.rationale: Repair of rejected trial-61aff8484b. That attempt replaced group 5621410346ca09a421d0 (three stage-4 [1,512,7,7]x[512,512,3,3] convolutions) with an im2col + cuBLAS-GEMM composite: quality passed (max_abs_error 3.9e-6, exact top-1, full coverage) but the paired project measurement regressed the objective from 1.446/1.453 ms to 4.863/4.941 ms (paired gains -3.416/-3.488 ms against MAD noise bounds 0.121/0.335 ms; rejected for paired_gain_not_above_noise and objective_not_improved). The measured lesson from that feedback is that per-call composite work (extra aten dispatches per site, an im2col kernel plus a skinny-N no-TF32 batched SGEMM route) can dominate kernel-time savings on this dispatch-sensitive batch=1 workload, so this attempt deliberately avoids multi-op composites. Following the repaired selection (group fc4ee42c1ef82b000685, single call faf88ed785916744a12ba5c9), the candidate replaces exactly one aten::conv2d signature - input [1,256,14,14] (stride (50176,196,14,1)), weight [512,256,3,3] (stride (2304,9,3,1)), bias None, stride [2,2], padding [1,1], dilation [1,1], groups 1 - with a single-launch custom FP32 CUDA implicit-GEMM kernel compiled at build time. Diagnostic evidence (target-resources.json): cuDNN's fixed heuristic (cudnn.benchmark frozen False) serves this call with one implicit_convolve_sgemm kernel launched as grid [2,16]xblock [8,8] = 32 CTAs / 2048 threads total, 80 registers/thread, 115.5 diagnostic CUDA us (~1.0 TFLOP/s FP32 for 115.6 MFLOP; 15.9% of the 727.7 us run total; the largest never-attempted leaf group). The replacement kernel launches grid (16,7) = 112 CTAs x 256 threads (28,672 threads vs 2,048 on a 128-SM device): each CTA owns 32 output channels of one output row, stages the three input rows that row touches (zero padding included) into 48 KB of shared memory once per CTA, and each thread computes one (output channel, output column) dot product over K=2304 with deterministic fmaf accumulation; weights are streamed through float4 loads from a one-per-model 16-byte-aligned [512,256,12] repack (taps 9..11 zero-padded) built at build time from the invariant module weight. No im2col buffer, no cuBLAS, no global torch/cudnn/cublas flag is touched, TF32 stays disabled, and the per-call CPU path is one guarded Python closure plus one C++ extension call (output allocation + one kernel launch inside), i.e. no more dispatch work than the parent aten::conv2d call it replaces. The equal-FLOP stride-2 sibling convolutions in the same forward pass run in ~30-36 us, which is the device-proven efficiency target for this FLOP budget; the kernel's index arithmetic was verified on CPU against F.conv2d (relative error ~4e-7, FP32 summation-order noise only), the extension compiles for sm_89, and a build-time randomized on-device self-check re-validates kernel plus packing before the fast path is enabled, degrading to the parent reference on any mismatch. Because the previous trial proved wall latency (~1.45 ms) exceeds total GPU busy time (~0.73 ms), the realized latency_ms gain may be smaller than the ~80-90 us kernel-time reduction, and acceptance is decided solely by the framework's paired AB/BA measurement against its noise bounds; if the single-kernel route does not clear them, the outcome is rejection rather than expansion into composites, per the selection.

setup_work.description: build() (1) optionally sanity-locates the owning module model.resnet.encoder.stages.3.layers.0.layer.0.convolution and verifies its weight is the contiguous FP32 CUDA [512,256,3,3] parameter (soft check; a miss only disables the fast path, it never widens semantics); (2) compiles one small CUDA extension (torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline, single kernel, no GPU execution at build other than step 4) - first compile is roughly 30-60 s of CPU nvcc work, cached on disk under the torch extensions directory so later workers/invocations reuse the .so; (3) packs the invariant weight once into a zero-padded float4-aligned [512,256,12] FP32 tensor retained for the model lifetime (6,291,456 bytes) - this is the only persistent allocation the candidate adds, and the runtime weight argument is still checked against the packed source pointer on every call, falling back to the parent op on any mismatch; (4) runs one randomized on-device self-check (private CPU generator, global RNG untouched): random [1,256,14,14] input and [512,256,3,3] weight, kernel output compared to F.conv2d at atol=rtol=1e-3 plus exact shape/stride/dtype/device checks, transients (~11.4 MB peak: 200KB input, 4.7MB weight, 6.3MB pack, two 100KB outputs) freed before returning; on any failure the fast path is disabled and the replacement behaves as the parent. No CUDA Graph capture, no allocator or memory-pool changes, no global torch/cudnn/cublas state modification, no parameter mutation (the original weight tensor is left untouched; the pack is an extra read-only copy), no fixture-dependent precomputation - the kernel consumes the live input tensor and the live weight identity on every invocation.
setup_work.setup_allocations: Retained for the model lifetime: 6,291,456 bytes (the [512,256,12] FP32 packed weight) on the model's device, plus the compiled extension .so on disk (no GPU memory). Transient during setup: ~11.4 MB peak from the self-check tensors, freed to the caching allocator before build() returns. This raises framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes/lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes by at most these amounts (setup is included in lifecycle counters); it is not a physical-memory saving claim.
setup_work.per_run_transients: Per replaced call the fast path allocates only the output [1,512,7,7] FP32 (100,352 bytes) through the caching allocator, exactly like the parent conv2d output; the input staging buffer is 48 KB of on-chip shared memory per CTA, not device memory, and no pools, graphs, or persistent buffers are created. framework.peak_allocated_bytes (reset per run) is therefore expected to be unchanged from the parent within normal allocator noise apart from the retained pack, which is charged at installation time rather than per run.

quality_risks: Numerics: the kernel accumulates each output dot product with sequential fmaf in a different order than cuDNN's implicit GEMM; both are pure FP32 with TF32 disabled. CPU verification of the exact index arithmetic against F.conv2d shows relative deviation ~4e-7 (ordinary summation-reorder noise), and the previously accepted-quality trial that reordered three convolutions measured 3.9e-6 max logit error against the atol=rtol=1e-4 gate, so this single reordered convolution is expected to stay comfortably inside tolerance; final acceptance still depends on the framework's paired quality check.

exact_top1 could flip only if the reference top-2 logits were separated by less than the induced perturbation (~1e-5 class); prior evidence (max_abs_error 3.9e-6 over 1001 logits when three convolutions were reordered) makes this negligible, and if it fails the framework restores the parent.

Toolchain risk: if nvcc/ninja compilation fails on the worker, or the build-time self-check fails or throws, the replacement silently degrades to calling the parent aten::conv2d reference with the original arguments for every signature - quality and semantics are preserved, only the speedup is lost, and coverage still counts the call through the replacement.

Guard scope: the fast path requires the exact observed shape/stride/dtype/device of both tensors, bias None, stride [2,2], padding [1,1], dilation [1,1], groups 1, the weight storage being the packed invariant parameter, and grad mode disabled for the weight; any other signature (or any exception inside the guard) falls back to the parent reference with original semantics, so autograd and unexpected shapes remain correct.

Memory counters: the retained 6.3 MB weight pack increases framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes (and possibly reserved) recorded from installation onward; per-run peak_allocated_bytes gains only the transient 100 KB output allocation identical to the parent call. No CUDA Graph pools are involved.
